correctness.rationale: For cubic graphs of order 2n, edge counting forces |D|≥n; equality holds precisely when every vertex has one neighbor across the cut. The finite-state graph on 4^(2k) vertices exhausts all local binary color patterns. The packaged exact code checks every transition and SCC: for k=1 two 1-cycles and one 4-cycle; for k=2 two 1-cycles and two 5-cycles. Closed-walk counts and the one-to-one correspondence with labelled sets prove the claimed formula for all n in each domain. Independently direct exhaustive assignment enumeration supports small n. No unproved infinite extrapolation is used.

originality.rationale: Prior papers prove the invariant, the half-order bound, and existence of the associated perfect two-colouring, but the inspected full primary sources do not classify/count every optimal vertex subset for both Petersen families. Strongly related 2026 Karami paper was accessible only by abstract; its possible unpublished exact enumerations remain a non-negligible historical priority risk.
residual_risks: Full text of arXiv:2606.14190v1 was not obtained; its authors may include exact-count arguments beyond the abstract.
Undiscovered perfect-colouring or cutting-bisection enumeration literature may subsume the named exact counts; no formal novelty guarantee.
The Petersen graph base case n=5 has six known perfect matchings, so that isolated base count alone is not novel.

value.rationale: The complete exact minimizer census for canonical cyclic cubic families exhibits nonconstant period-four and period-five arithmetic jumps while the minimum domination size remains n. Every optimal vertex subset is classified by explicit periodic words, providing a structurally usable answer rather than merely proving existence or recomputing a generic bound.
